answer: CD14 Mono (classical monocytes) — the immune cell type with the highest number of significantly differentially expressed genes after AAV9 mini-dystrophin treatment, with 315 significant DEGs at p_val_adj < 0.05 (out of 316 genes tested, 99.7%), far ahead of runner-up CD16 Mono (240). The result is robust to a stricter threshold (314 significant at p_val_adj < 0.01, still #1) and to counting up-regulated genes only (152, still #1); only under a down-regulation-only criterion does the ranking flip (CD16 Mono 181 vs CD14 Mono 163). Large-gene-count cell types (Eryth 3,142, pDC 2,519, Plasmablast 2,292 tested) had zero significant DEGs, so the winner is not an artifact of panel size.
